The failure was only a quoting issue, not a mathematical result. I’m switching to a one-line state enumeration so the shell receives valid code, and I’ll include the end-of-ramp drain explicitly.
```python
calc_output = await run_command("node -e 'const N=100,hit=Array(N+1).fill(0);let d=new Map([[\"1,2,3|4\",1]]);while(d.size){let nd=new Map();for(const [key,pr] of d){let z=key.split(\"|\"),s=z[0].split(\",\").map(x=>x===\"\"?null:(x===\"null\"?null:+x)),k=+z[1];for(let p=0;p<3;p++){if(s[p]!=null)hit[s[p]]+=pr/3;let ns,nk;if(p===0){ns=[s[1],s[2],k<=N?k:null];nk=k+1}else if(p===1){ns=[s[2],k<=N?k:null,k+1<=N?k+1:null];nk=k+2}else{ns=[s[1],k<=N?k:null,k+1<=N?k+1:null];nk=k+2}if(ns.some(x=>x!=null)){let q=ns.join(\",\")+\"|\"+nk;nd.set(q,(nd.get(q)||0)+pr/3)}}}d=nd}let b=1;for(let i=2;i<=N;i++)if(hit[i]>hit[b])b=i;console.log(JSON.stringify({best:b,probability:hit[b],top:[...Array(N)].map((_,j)=>[j+1,hit[j+1]]).sort((a,c)=>c[1]-a[1]).slice(0,10),total:hit.reduce((a,x)=>a+x,0)}))'") 
print(calc_output)
```
5
